meta.title: Circular vs linear convolution: the wrap-around error
meta.tools: DFT-domain multiplication without padding, time-domain aliasing analysis, padding sweep
meta.summary: Show that multiplying DFTs without enough padding computes a circular convolution, predict exactly which output samples are corrupted and by how much (the tail wraps onto the head), and find the minimum FFT size that eliminates the error.
meta.problem: An FFT-based filter output looks wrong at the start of each block. Why, and how much padding is enough?
meta.theory:
With DFT size L, $\mathrm{IDFT}(X_LH_L)[n]=\sum_k y_{lin}[n+kL]$ — the linear result aliased in time with period L. For lengths N and M, samples $n < N+M-1-L$ receive the wrapped tail; the
error there equals exactly $y_{lin}[n+L]$. Error vanishes iff L ≥ N+M−1.
meta.method: x = 64 random samples, h = 16-tap smoothing filter (N+M−1 = 79). L from 64 to 96. Error of the circular result vs the linear one, compared sample-by-sample with the predicted wrapped tail.
meta.track: Applied Mathematics — 218 projects in electrical engineering

rows.quantity: Error equals the wrapped tail y_lin[n+L], worst mismatch over all L
Smallest L with zero wrap-around error = N+M−1
